mt: 'VIAF' ON THE OVERVIEW — THE AUTHORITY FILE AT ITS GRAIN, ORIGIN AND OPERATOR EXACT; PSEUDONYMS LINKED; THE CLUSTER IDENTIFIER GIVEN AS 'UNIQUE', WHERE THE SAVED ACCOUNT HAS IT COALESCE AND SPLIT
d: THE FILE, SIGNED OUT, 2026-11-01: 'The Virtual International Authority File (VIAF) is an international name authority service that combines multiple national library authority files into a single online database.' Key Features: operator (OCLC); origin (1998, Library of Congress, DNB, OCLC; 'launching formally in August 2003'); purpose ('linking variant names, pseudonyms, and corporate titles'); integration ('Each cluster receives a unique standard identifier/URI'); access. Six cards: VIAF, OCLC (two), Wikipedia, the LOD Cloud, the Semantic Web Journal.
reading: The innocent reading first. Asked for the acronym, the Overview says what the file is, who runs it, where it came from, what it is for and how to use it.
findings: ORIGIN AND OPERATOR EXACT. 'Initiated in 1998 as a joint proof-of-concept by the U.S. Library of Congress, the German National Library (DNB), and OCLC' follows the saved article ('initiated by the American Library of Congress (LC), the German National Library (DNB), and the OCLC in April 1998 as a proof-of-concept that authority records can be linked'); 'launching formally in August 2003' answers to the consortium formed at the 2003 World Library and Information Congress 'on 6 August 2003,'. The fourth card carries the OCLC transition 'on April 4, 2012', the article's 'The project transitioned to being a service of OCLC on 4 April 2012.'

PSEUDONYMS LINKED. 'Solves author name disambiguation by linking variant names, pseudonyms, and corporate titles across different languages, scripts, and regional spelling rules.' The saved article says a record 'contains the primary "see" and "see also" records from the original documents'; it names no pseudonyms, and the census row records that it 'does not say how a pseudonym or heteronym is held, as a see or see-also form of one cluster or as a cluster of its own'. The composition's linking of pseudonyms is on no saved page. Borgman's point that VIAF 'is led by libraries, as opposed to individual authors or creators' is not carried.

THE UNIQUE IDENTIFIER AND THE MONTHLY CLUSTERS. 'Each cluster receives a unique standard identifier/URI'. The article: 'VIAF's clustering algorithm is run every month. As more data are added from participating libraries, clusters of authority records may coalesce or split, leading to some fluctuation in the VIAF identifier of certain authority records.' The census reads that fluctuation as the point where an authorial name can be merged with another by algorithm or separated again; the composition presents the identifier as stable. The integration into 'Wikipedia biographical articles, and Wikidata' matches the article ('The file numbers are also being added to Wikipedia biographical articles and are incorporated into Wikidata').

THE PARTICIPANTS. The answer names no participating file beyond the three founders; the LOD Cloud card gives 'joint project of 20 national libraries', a figure in no saved source. The article's list includes ISNI, the Getty ULAN and 'Wikidata [ citation needed ] WKP'. The census row's lifecycle note stands: viaf.org refused the fetch, and the composition's VIAF card ('VIAF: The Virtual International Authority File ...') is the only trace here of the site's own page.
analysis: The authority file composed accurately on origin, operator and integration. On names it states a linkage of pseudonyms the saved source does not, and it gives the cluster identifier as unique where the source records its fluctuation.
per_note: OCLC named as operator, the Library of Congress and DNB as initiators; no example identifier; sources carded.

atoms.reference: An international authority file linking the national authority files into a single virtual authority file, identical records from different data sets linked together.

evidence.record_quote: The Virtual International Authority File ( VIAF ) is an international authority file . It is a joint project of several national libraries, operated by the Online Computer Library Center (OCLC).

The aim is to link the national authority files (such as the German Integrated Authority File ) to a single virtual authority file. In this file, identical records from the different data sets are linked together.

atoms.reference: Authority records from participants among them the Library of Congress NACO, ISNI, the Getty Union List of Artist Names and Wikidata (citation needed).

evidence.record_quote: After several failed attempts to develop a unique joint authority file, the new idea was to link existing national authorities.

atoms.reference: The data made available online for research, data exchange and sharing; reciprocal updating by OAI-PMH.

evidence.record_quote: The data is made available online and is available for research and, data exchange and sharing. Reciprocal updating uses the Open Archives Initiative Protocol for Metadata Harvesting (OAI-PMH) protocol.
